transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-12
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~78 minutes (recording truncated at 1:18)
Attendees: Jared Bowman, Priya Raman, Lena Ortiz, Noah Kim, Marcus Lee

Summary: quick tabletop to walk through an 'escape hatch' for serving - staged degradation modes, canary traffic, and manual rollback triggers. Focus on what the oncall does, what telemetry we need, and communication templates.

Topics: escape hatch concepts; circuit breakers; canary simulation; degraded feature sets (no streaming, reduced max tokens, cache-first routing); runbook owners and SLAs; communication and escalation path.

[00:00] Jared: alright let's get started. thanks everybody for joining the tabletop, this is purposefully short, we want to run a few scenarios — canary fails, mem pressure, and rpc backlog. goal is a clear escape hatch and who does what.
[00:18] Priya: yeah, i'll kick off with the mem pressure case — staging looked fine but we saw a 2x p95, and the kv cache bloated. i want to confirm the steps for staged degradation, like first turn on prefix cache only, then reduce max tokens, then route to lower-cost model.
[00:38] Lena: and product wants the user experience to be predictable — if we drop streaming we should warn clients, have a header or status code so SDKs can react.
[00:52] Noah: cross-talk — when you say "prefix cache only" do you mean we evict the kv for long context or we only use prefix hits? i'm not sure our current cache policy supports partial mode.
[01:12] Marcus: the runtime has a flag 'serve_cached_prefixes' we can flip, it reduces KV lookups but you still need to limit the kv size. it's a bit hand wavy in the code base, i'll add a better toggle.
[01:30] Priya: ok so checklist for mem pressure scenario: 1) set serve_cached_prefixes=true, 2) lower max_context from 8k to 2k, 3) enable model-variant fallback (quantized variant).
[01:47] Jared: and who executes that? oncall or ops? in prod we need a clear owner.
[01:54] Priya: oncall does the toggle, infra (Marcus) owns the model variant rollout small risk windows.
[02:08] Lena: we should document exact CLI/Console clicks — i.e., console path: Routes -> Model policies -> Fallback -> enable 'quantized-variant-1' and set weight 30%. put the exact screenshot in the runbook.
[02:28] Noah: small note: when we've done ad-hoc fallback in the past the trace ids didn't propagate properly, so tracing/observability must be included. otherwise it's impossible to tell what requests hit the fallback.
[02:45] Marcus: noted — need a flag in the trace that says 'fallback=true' and the model hash. i'll add that to the telemetry spike.
[02:55] Jared: next scenario — canary fails to converge. we roll canary to 10% traffic, latency doubles and error budget starts draining. what's the escape?
[03:12] Priya: immediate action: pause the canary rollout (console stop), switch routing to safe model (pinned previous stable), and if p95 > SLO for 2 consecutive minutes, trigger the circuit break that returns 503s to non-critical paths.
[03:32] Lena: product question: what are non-critical paths? search rerank vs core conversation? need to call those out — otherwise teams will be surprised.
[03:43] Jared: agreed. for rollout we add labels: critical=true/false in route config so fallback can apply differently. also update SDK to surface the 503 reason.
[03:56] Noah: regarding the circuit breaker — how do we avoid all-outage when external retries kick in? some clients will retry and multiply traffic.
[04:12] Priya: we need token buckets & rate limiting that are reactive to downstream errors. add a strict backoff header to responses so smart clients back off.
[04:24] Marcus: that header idea is good; we can set x-rw-backoff: 30s and the SDK will backoff. but third-party clients won't respect it. we should also add a route-level retry policy in the ingress.
[04:40] [interrupt] Lena: quick thought — we also want golden metrics to show when fallback hits. add a dashboard tile for 'fallback requests %' and 'kv cache hit rate' and 'avg model latency fallback vs normal'.
[04:55] Jared: action: Priya + Marcus to add tiles.
[05:03] Priya: capturing, will add with a target of 2026-10-15.
[05:10] Jared: scenario 3 — RPC backlog from client-side misuse (fanout). we get request storms, scheduling queue grows, and the scheduler OOMs on batches.
[05:24] Noah: we've seen this in experiments — big seq lengths + massive mini-batches blow memory. escape hatch is to limit batch size and disable long-context scheduling. but that increases latency.
[05:38] Marcus: runtime knob: 'max_batch_tokens' and 'max_batch_items' — set conservatively when we detect queue depth > threshold. this is automatic currently but we need a manual override.
[05:52] Priya: i want a manual 'protect mode' for oncall with a one-click in console: disables streaming, reduces batch size, moves to quantized variant, flips serve_cached_prefixes. that should give us breathing room.
[06:07] Lena: and product should define acceptable UX degradation states: A) Degraded (no streaming, lower fidelity), B) Restricted (read-only type calls), C) Emergency (return 503 for low-priority).
[06:22] Jared: good — map these states to exact console operations. we'll call them 'Degraded', 'Restricted', 'Emergency'.
[06:30] [10 min silence recorded? no — small cross chatter]
[06:45] Noah: telemetry discussion — we need end-to-end trace ids, fallback flag, model-hash, and batch-size in logs. also, we should log the active policy set that caused the fallback.
[07:02] Marcus: agree, also we need to instrument the scheduler to emit sample latencies per sequence length bucket — 128/512/2k. that helps us set safe thresholds.
[07:18] Lena: compliance note — for Private/VPC customers we need to ensure our escape hatch steps don't violate data residency. if we route to a fallback model that's hosted in a different region that's a problem.
[07:33] Priya: yes, for private deployments the playbook should be region-aware and list approved fallback models per region. we'll add a section in the runbook.
[07:45] Jared: security & audit: every escape-hatch toggle must create an audit log entry and a postmortem ticket with root cause template. Marcus, can you add automatic ticket creation?
[07:58] Marcus: yeah we can wire a webhook to jira that fires on policy change and attaches runtime metrics snapshot. i'll prototype.
[08:10] Noah: re: canary simulation — i propose we build a harness that replays production traces at scaled qps into staging and runs the escape hatch automations. this will exercise telemetry, dashboards, and runbooks.
[08:27] Priya: timeline — canary sim by 2026-10-20, need runbook draft earlier so oncall knows where to click.
[08:38] Jared: ok let's walk through the runbook steps live — Priya, can you narrate the mem pressure path?
[08:45] Priya: step 1: open console -> infra -> live policies. step 2: set 'protect mode' (the one-click), step 3: confirm telemetry snapshot exported, step 4: switch traffic weights to fallback model 30% then 0% if unstable. step 5: notify stakeholders — runbook has templates.
[09:05] Lena: do we want an automated rollback after a timeout? or always manual?
[09:12] Jared: prefer an operator-confirmed rollback, but we can allow an automatic rollback guard if errors drop below threshold for 5 minutes. make it configurable.
[09:23] Marcus: implementation detail — the automatic rollback requires a stable snapshot, but if the canary failed due to cold cache we might get false positives. need guard rails.
[09:36] Noah: for the notification flow: slack channel #prod-incident, oncall sends the standard message and pins the runbook link, adds the run id. templates should include a short blurb and expanded details.
[09:52] Lena: product will author the message templates; i'll own that.
[09:58] Jared: good. any legal/compliance considerations? i think SOC 2 needs the audit logs, retention, and change authorization.
[10:08] Priya: confirm: we currently persist policy changes for 90 days in the audit log. if legal wants longer we need to discuss retention tier.
[10:17] Marcus: and kube / infra-level changes need two-person approval for private deployments - that must be in the runbook.
[10:27] Jared: ok let's capture a sample degraded mode SLA: we still meet critical path p99 < 1.5x baseline for 5 minutes after toggles; non-critical can return 503. that's our target and we should doc it.
[10:45] [pause]
[10:50] Priya: edge case — what about model stateful sessions (KV cache) when we switch variants? we risk cache mismatch. we should prefer fallbacks that accept same KV schema.
[11:05] Marcus: note: quantized variant maintains the same kv layout in 90% of models we onboarded; i'll verify per-model. add a checklist to model onboarding: 'verify kv schema compatibility for fallback variants'.
[11:20] Noah: ops question: who declares the incident over? oncall or product?
[11:27] Lena: product signs off on service degradation being acceptable, but oncall declares technical resolution. final incident close requires postmortem with both.
[11:40] Jared: good. let's run a quick tabletop: mem pressure -> we flip protect mode -> fallback -> telemetry shows 40% fallback -> latency returns to acceptable level -> we draft postmortem. who goes first? Noah run it.
[11:55] Noah: starting simulation walkthrough: console click protect mode -> confirm -> toggle fallback variant -> watch dashboard — fallback % climbs to 40, p95 drops from 1.2s to 0.9s. if p95 remains > SLO for 3 min, trigger emergency.
[12:20] Priya: side note — we should document how to manually scale dedicated pools if dedicated is the customer tier. different toggle there: "reserved-capacity-resize" not quick in console.
[12:34] Marcus: yeah dedicated pools need infra action; include steps and contact matrix for Dedicated customers.
[12:45] Lena: next, communication plan: product will create 3 templates — internal incident, external degraded-UX, and customer-notice (for dedicated/private). include expected timeline and rollback blurb.
[13:00] Jared: ok, we are at the last 10 minutes, quick recap and owners.
[13:06] Priya: recap: create v1 runbook and 'protect mode' UI + telemetry tiles. timeline: tiles & circuit-breaker telemetry 10/15, runbook 10/16, canary sim 10/20.
[13:20] Marcus: i'll prototype audit webhook and fallback trace flag by 10/15.
[13:27] Lena: templates by 10/16, product will QA with comms.
[13:33] Noah: i'll get the canary harness and simulation scripts ready for 10/20 and loop in performance.
[13:40] Jared: perfect. any final questions?
[13:44] [brief silence]
[13:50] Lena: just one: should we include a 'kill switch' that returns a friendly status page to end-users? might be useful.
[13:58] Priya: we can add an 'incident mode' that surfaces a friendly banner on the hosted console and an explanatory header to API responses.
[14:10] Jared: wrap up — i will consolidate notes and assign action items in jira. we will run the canary sim on the 20th. thanks everyone.

Recorded notes (imperfect transcription): occasional overlaps, some product names misheard ("redwood dedicate" for Dedicated), shorthand and a few cut words.
